messages:
maya: Heads up — customer tenant_netx-42 reporting huge spike in 5xx/timeouts from hosted API starting ~08:12 UTC. Lots of p95/p99 tail timeouts and 504s. They say it started after a large ingest job + steady traffic. Can someone triage? cc @ryan-oncall @sasha

incident-bot: ALERT: hosted.request_queue.depth > 900 for 90s (08:13:02) — severity=page

ryan-oncall: grabbing dashboards now. which model/region? any recent deploys?

maya: model=open-llama-70b (hosted-eu-west), tenant is on shared pool but with reserved flags. recent runtime roll 1.12 (quantization) landed yesterday. payloads include long contexts (customer uploads ~120k tokens in chunks). They repro locally with a short script.

sasha: ok — long contexts + continuous batching is a risky combo. can you dump a sample request and one of the failing request_ids?

maya: sample request (sanitized):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-70b","input":"<very long context>\",\"max_tokens\":512}'
```
failed request_id: rq_20240314_84ab

lee: checking autoscaler + quota. saw no new nodes spin up for that pool — autoscaler decision returned "no-scale" due to reserved_capacity flag combo. grabbing logs from pool-hosted-7.

omar: looking at batcher metrics. continuous-batcher backlog shot to 520 pending batches. KV cache size for the model jumped to 6.2GB and eviction wasn't kicking in quickly. my suspicion: long sequences are preventing normal batch churn -> large kv-cache growth -> batcher threads slow -> queue depth increases -> early_reject then 502/504s.

-- log snippet from host ip-10-2-3-44 --
```
[08:12:14] queue_depth=1032 tenant=tenant_netx-42 batcher_pending=512 continuous_kvsize=6.2GB p95=4.2s p99=14.8s errors=504
[08:12:46] batcher_window_ms=200 kv_evictions=0 mem_free=1.1GB
```

ryan-oncall: confirmed. ingress shows burst ~250rps for ~90s then steadied to 60rps. backlog correlates with the ingest window.

sasha: can we repro in staging to validate mitigation? maybe force-short circuit kv-cache for that tenant.

maya: customer agreed to pause bulk ingest at 08:22 UTC while we triage.

ryan-oncall: proposed mitigations (temporary):
1) reduce continuous-batcher window from 200ms -> 50ms for impacted pool
2) lower early_reject threshold from 1024 -> 800 for hosted to shed earlier
3) flip tenant to smaller-model fallback for new requests (open-llama-7b)
4) restart batcher-worker on ip-10-2-3-44 to flush stuck batches

lee: rolled window change to pool-hosted-7 (canary 1/3) at 08:24 — watching metrics.

omar: pushed kv-cache eviction TTL policy to batcher instance 3 (immediate, non-rolling) at 08:25. also triggered a soft restart of the batcher process.

incident-bot: ACTION: mitigation_applied {"pool":"pool-hosted-7","changes":"batcher_window=50ms,kv_ttl_enforced,restart"} — 08:25:18

tara-cs: letting customer know we applied mitigations and asking them to keep ingest paused for 15m. customer replied: "paused, will wait for update".

maya: after mitigations p95 dropped from ~4.2s -> ~900ms within 3 minutes; p99 still ~6-8s but errors decreased by ~85%. queue_depth now hovering ~420.

sasha: good sign. still want a repro and a root cause. omar — any corollary in the 1.12 quantization change?

omar: nothing obvious in the quant kernels. this looks primarily operational: our kv-cache policy didn't expect these very long, high-retention sequences; combined with batcher window at 200ms it amplified. quantization may have slightly increased per-token CPU but not the dominant factor.

ryan-oncall: immediate next steps:
- keep tenant ingest paused until p99 < 2s for 15m (assigned: maya)
- add per-tenant long-context rate limit (short-term) (assigned: lee)
- add alert for continuous_kvsize growth and auto-evict threshold (assigned: omar)
- run a staging repro of the exact burst pattern and long-context to validate fixes (assigned: sasha)

maya: customer agreed to extend pause until we confirm stable metrics. will update on status.

lee: filing a follow-up ticket and will request quota exception for this tenant if they need sustained capacity.

omar: action item to review default batcher_window and KV cache defaults for long-context models. target PR by EOD.

sasha: I'll try to reproduce in staging with the exact request generator and confirm that fallback + window change resolves tail timeouts.

maya: final status for now — mitigations working, customer unblocked for now but we need the long-term changes.

-- Postmortem TODOs (quick list) --
- enforce per-tenant rate limits for large-context uploads
- expose continuous_kvsize alert and auto-evict
- revisit default continuous-batcher window & early_reject thresholds
- add smart-fallback routing when queue_depth spikes

owners: lee, omar, sasha (see tickets created)

ryan-oncall: thanks everyone. will keep this thread updated with PR links and timing for rollout.

maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
